BiblicalUsage: Mahir means quick, ready, skilful, and it marks the man whose gift is ready to hand. Ezra 7:6 calls Ezra a ready scribe in the law of Moses, and Proverbs 22:29 says a man diligent in his business shall stand before kings. Psalms 45:1 says the psalmist's tongue is the pen of a ready writer.
TheologicalSignificance: I believe this word ties skill to standing: the diligent man in Proverbs 22:29 stands before kings because his gift was ready when the king needed it. My position is that Ezra in Ezra 7:6 shows where readiness comes from, because the hand of the LORD his God was upon him.
